species.look_here_first: Look where the leaf stalk meets the stem: flowers and long, pointed seed capsules arise there. Check the capsule ribs together with the palmately lobed, toothed leaves.
morphology_keys: Upright herb with stiff hairs on stems and leaves.
Leaves have several palmately arranged lobes and toothed edges.
Flower has a fused stamen column; slender epicalyx bracts sit outside the calyx.
Elongated capsules usually have five ribs and split when mature.
species.remaining_comparison: Compare with other cultivated Abelmoschus and hibiscus-like mallows; source-backed local comparison remains pending.
photo_roles: Habit with leaf attachment and fruit positions visible.
Side view of an attached capsule showing its ribs and pointed tip.
Flower side and center showing epicalyx bracts, calyx and stamen column.

species.look_here_first: Turn over a leaflet and inspect its base. Look for blunt teeth bearing raised glands; most of the remaining leaflet edge is smooth. Confirm with the whole compound leaf and, when present, winged fruits.
morphology_keys: Large compound leaves carry numerous leaflets.
Leaflet margins are mostly smooth except for gland-bearing teeth near the base.
Winged fruits have a seed near the middle of the twisted wing.
species.remaining_comparison: Black walnut and many sumacs have serrations along much more of the leaflet edge. Inspect margin and basal glands together; retain source-specific comparison rather than a universal claim about every sumac.
photo_roles: Complete compound leaf with attachment to twig.
Underside macro of leaflet-base teeth and glands.
Attached fruit cluster and one individual winged fruit.

species.look_here_first: Examine the large, heart-shaped leaf and its velvety hair covering, then find the branched flower cluster and a mature segmented fruit. Use the fruit and flower structure along with the leaves.
morphology_keys: Shrubby growth with large, soft-haired, heart-shaped leaves.
Five-petaled flowers are borne in branched clusters.
Mature dry fruit separates into seed-bearing segments.
species.remaining_comparison: Exact separating characters against Abutilon and Wissadula require a sourced comparison before adding an identification key.
photo_roles: Branch showing leaf attachment and the branched flower cluster.
Both leaf surfaces with hair detail.
Flower center and side view.
Mature fruit and separated segments with a scale.

species.look_here_first: Separate the central spadix from the surrounding pleated spathe. This is a cluster of tiny flowers, not one enormous flower. Also document the separate, tree-like leaf stage.
morphology_keys: Large flowering structure consists of a spadix surrounded by a spathe.
Actual flowers occupy the lower part of the spadix.
A large divided leaf is borne on a stalk during the leaf stage.
species.remaining_comparison: Compare with other cultivated Amorphophallus; size or smell alone cannot establish species. Require exact accession/observation identity.
photo_roles: Whole inflorescence with scale.
Spathe and spadix junction; lower flower zones only if already visible without damage.
Whole leaf and its branching pattern.

species.look_here_first: Find the narrow spathe and the long, slender spadix extending beyond it. Then examine the complete divided leaf above it, not a single leaflet.
morphology_keys: Usually one large compound leaf with multiple leaflets.
Slender spadix extends well beyond the narrow spathe.
Fruits form a cluster that becomes red.

comparison_update.text: Compare Pinellia pedatisecta using its disproportionately large central leaflet and inflorescence above leaves; Arisaema dracontium has more similar-sized leaflets and a mostly below-leaf inflorescence. Other Arisaema complex comparisons remain pending.

species.remaining_comparison: NC State distinguishes Pinellia pedatisecta by its disproportionately large central leaflet and inflorescence above the leaves. Final regional Arisaema-complex key and photo identity remain pending.
photo_roles: Whole leaf with all leaflets visible.
Inflorescence profile showing spadix extension and its position relative to the leaf.

species.look_here_first: Look for the four conspicuous wings of the mature fruiting unit. Confirm the shrubby habit and small, grayish, scaly leaves; foliage alone is insufficient.
morphology_keys: Woody shrub with alternate simple leaves.
Leaves have a grayish surface with small scales.
Mature fruiting units show four prominent wings.

comparison_update.text: Use the four prominent wings on fruiting bracts with narrow gray leaves; a sterile shrub alone is insufficient. Do not assign a variety from these species-level photographs.

species.look_here_first: Follow the slender flower spikes back to the leaf axils. Check the usually opposite, toothed leaves and their prominent lengthwise veins together with those spikes.
morphology_keys: Herbaceous perennial with usually opposite leaves.
Leaves have coarse teeth and conspicuous veins.
Tiny flowers cluster along slender axillary spikes.
species.remaining_comparison: Resembles stinging nettles, but Boehmeria lacks their stinging hairs. Do not use touch as an identification test. Regional nettle comparison remains pending.
photo_roles: Node with leaf pair and attached flower spike.

species.look_here_first: Check the open, nodding panicle and an individual floret. Photograph the bent, twisted awn and hairy floret base, then the papery ligule where blade meets sheath.
morphology_keys: Annual grass with an open, branched panicle and hanging spikelets.
Collar has a membranous ligule and no auricles.
Floret has a prominent basal callus, stiff basal hairs, and a bent, twisted awn.
species.remaining_comparison: Do not equate every oat-like panicle with A. fatua; distinguish other Avena with a regional floret key. UC IPM lists hare barley and ripgut brome as seedling confusers.
photo_roles: Panicle with pendant spikelets.
Separated mature floret showing basal callus and awn attachment, with millimeter scale.
Collar macro showing ligule and lack of auricles.
species.blocker: Downloaded panicle/spikelet photos lack mature disarticulation, callus and floret details needed to exclude other Avena. NEEDS_FIRST_PHOTO with mature-floret evidence.
species.next_action: Resolve stated photo blocker; preserve prior taxonomic decisions.

species.look_here_first: Follow a low leafy shoot to a tiny flower head. Check opposite hairy leaves, then examine the overlapping bracts beneath the head and the barbed awns on mature fruits.
morphology_keys: Low perennial with opposite, toothed, simple leaves.
Small heads combine ray and disk florets.
Mature flattened fruits bear unequal, barbed awns.
species.remaining_comparison: Compare low lawn Asteraceae using head underside and mature fruits; exact local confuser key remains pending. Small yellow flowers alone are insufficient.
photo_roles: Whole creeping shoot and an attached opposite leaf pair.
Head from above and below with millimeter scale.
Mature fruits showing the unequal awns under magnification.

species.look_here_first: Start at the basal clump of narrow, keeled leaves and follow the flowering stalk upward. Photograph a six-parted flower and the three-chambered fruit rather than relying on flower color.
morphology_keys: Bulb-forming perennial with basal linear leaves.
Flowers occur along an elongated raceme.
